newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish pound dips below 0.9200 as sterling rallies.
newsitem.headline: Irish pound dips below 0.9200 as sterling rallies.

text.p: The Irish pound dipped below 0.9200 sterling in midday trade on Tuesday as the UK currency rallied to its strongest level since August 1992 following a UK rate rise and the announcement of greater independence for the Bank of England.

Dealers said the announcement by Gordon Brown, Britain's new Chancellor of the Exchequer, that he was giving the Bank of England operational responsibility for setting interest rates was warmly welcomed in the market.
"He said the right things. He placated any nerves that might have been there and he's looking for solid growth with low inflation," Pat O'Sullivan, economist at AIB Group Treasury told Reuters.
The announcement, coupled with the rate rise, pushed sterling to a four and a half year high against the mark but dealers said the Irish pound held in reasonably well against a surging British unit.
By 1125 GMT, the Irish pound was at 0.9190 sterling against 0.9255 before the rate rise and a high of 0.9285 this morning.

Dealers believe sterling should remain strong in the short-term, bolstered by expectations of another 25 to 50 basis point rise in UK rates but they do not expect to see the Irish pound slip below 0.9100 sterling.
"I don't think we'll see it breaking below 0.9100. There should be good support for it around that level," said one trader.
The punt firmed to 2.5970 marks from 2.5925 before the UK rate announcement as the absence of any selling pressure allowed it to track sterling/mark higher.
But dealers warned that selling pressure could re-emerge above 2.60 marks.
"Obviously if sterling goes higher and mark/Irish is dragged up with it, then you are in danger of recreating the kind of conditions that prevailed last week," AIB's O'Sullivan said.
